key_insight: PACT shows that token-level credit can be uniquely defined by three regularity conditions, then uses this theory to improve actor-critic training via better critic alignment.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more principled way to train LLM agents and reasoning systems by aligning critic updates with the post-update policy, improving stability and accuracy.
method: Define token-level credit with Completeness, Prefix Consistency, and Neutrality.
Interpret OPD, RLOO, and GAE through the lens of expected policy-gradient contributions from token credit.
Use Actor-then-Critic training with importance sampling correction to align the critic with the updated policy.
evidence_signal: PACT reports 72.87% average accuracy across four mathematical reasoning benchmarks and a 67.4% pass rate on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming PPO, GRPO, and SAO in the abstract.
watch_item: The actor-then-critic update relies on importance sampling correction, which can be sensitive to policy shift and may require careful tuning in practice.
paper_title: PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment
